messages:
alex: FYI customer report — sudden spike of 429s during a short traffic burst. They say latency was fine for minutes then many requests started failing with quota errors. Pasted logs below.
maria: Can you drop the customer request_id and a small repro? also which route/model are they on?
alex: route: /v1/generate, model: rdx-mini-01, quota_id: cust-8472. Sample headers from failing call:
```
x-rw-req-id: req_9a2b
x-rate-limit-status: quota_exceeded
x-rl-remaining: 0
x-rl-reset: 30
```
They reported cache_warmup around the burst window in our telemetry.
priya: Interesting — might be interplay between continuous batching and KV cache cold-start. If prefix cache misses cause upstream runtime to hold tokens while filling batches, burst of new prefixes could blow through quota tokens quickly and look like throttling.
jordan: Do we see batch_hold_ms spike around the same time? ops-bot, can you paste the trace?
ops-bot: Trace snippets for req_9a2b:
```
batching.delay_ms: 45
kvcache.hit: false
kvcache.prefetch: false
tokens_generated: 320
server_latency_ms: 210
```
maria: That batching.delay_ms isn't huge but if many parallel requests all miss kvcache and end up generating tokens, the per-token quota burn is higher than expected — client thinks we throttled them when quota was just exhausted.
alex: Customer asserts they didn't send more QPS than usual — it was a short burst of new user sessions (new prefixes). They saw almost immediate 429s after ~10 successful calls.
priya: Two hypotheses: 1) quota accounting is per-token and a cold cache leads to more tokens consumed (lower cache hit => more total work), 2) continuous batching introduces a short head-of-line wait that concentrates requests into few served batches causing burst-like accounting. Either way, perceived throttling.
jordan: Repro plan: ask customer to run controlled test — send 30 requests with new random prefixes and capture x-rl-* headers, and another run using a warmup (seed prefixes to prefill kvcache) and compare. Also capture batch_hold_ms and kvcache.hit in response metadata.
alex: I asked them for the repro and gave them a small curl that includes a unique prefix generator. Sent them guidance to set an env var to force immediate send (disable batching) for their test client if possible.
maria: Short-term mitigation we can offer: 1) raise their short-window quota for the route temporarily, 2) enable a small prefetch for popular prefixes, 3) set route fallback to a lower-cost model with no batching for burst paths.
priya: Notes for engineering follow-up:
- Check quota burn accounting when kvcache.hit == false; verify tokens counted per request vs per effective generated tokens.
- Add telemetry to correlate kvcache hit-rate, batch sizes, and x-rl-remaining in a single trace view.
- Consider smoothing burst accounting by slightly delaying quota decrement until end-of-batch (to avoid concentrated hits?) — need product input.
jordan: For immediate ops action I've temporarily bumped cust-8472 short-window token bucket by +5000 tokens and added a canary route that disables continuous batching. Customer confirmed fewer 429s after change.
alex: Customer follow-up: after we bumped quota + canary, errors dropped to near zero for 20 min. They want a recommendation to avoid this in prod — I suggested warming common prefixes + backoff/retry with jitter + consider dedicated capacity for sustained bursts.
maria: Good. Create a short internal runbook entry about "KV-cache cold-start + continuous batching can appear like quota exhaustion" and include repro steps. Priya, can you own the item to add the telemetry correlation?
priya: Yep I'll take it. I'll also open a small experiment to try delayed quota decrement vs per-request accounting and check side effects.
alex: I'll close with the customer this afternoon and share the reproducible logs and our temporary fixes. :thumbsup:
